scriptural_facts.text: Jerusalem was a great city, and prophets warned that it must be destroyed unless the people repented.
The city had walls; Nephi's brothers hid outside them by night while he crept into the city.

visual_design_choices: A walled hilltop city of Judah around 600 BC, crowded with flat-roofed houses of honey-colored limestone stepping down terraced slopes.
Thick pale stone walls with square towers and a large arched gate; narrow stepped streets and small courtyards.
Surrounded by olive groves and terraced hills under a bright blue sky, with warm golden sunlight on the stone.
Old World Near Eastern architecture, not Mesoamerican: this is Judah, not the promised land.
locked_traits: Honey-colored limestone, flat roofs, and walls with square towers in every panel.
Judean Iron Age architecture only; no domes, minarets, pyramids, or later buildings.

scriptural_facts.text: Lehi had his own house at Jerusalem.
He left behind his house, the land of his inheritance, his gold, silver, and precious things.

visual_design_choices: A comfortable two-story limestone courtyard house of a well-off Judean family, around 600 BC.
An open central courtyard with a fig tree, a stone cistern, clay storage jars, and a wooden ladder to the flat roof.
Interior rooms with woven rugs, a low wooden bed with wool blankets, oil lamps in wall niches.
Bright sunlight falling into the courtyard; warm cream walls and blue sky overhead.
locked_traits: Same courtyard, fig tree, and cream limestone walls in every panel.
Well-off but not palatial: no columns of marble or royal decoration.

scriptural_facts.text: Nephi went by night through the city toward the house of Laban.
Laban had a treasury, kept by a servant who held its keys.

visual_design_choices: A large, imposing Jerusalem residence of a powerful man, with high limestone walls and a heavy cedar gate bound in bronze.
Inside, a colonnaded courtyard of dressed stone and a separate treasury room with a strong wooden door and iron lock.
The treasury holds shelves of sealed jars, rolled records, and chests; the brass plates rest there.
Usually seen by night: deep blue moonlight with warm amber torchlight at the gate, still clear and readable.
locked_traits: Same cedar-and-bronze gate and colonnaded courtyard in every panel.
Grander than Lehi's house; Judean architecture, never Roman or medieval.

scriptural_facts.text: Fleeing Laban's servants into the wilderness, the brothers hid in the cavity of a rock.

visual_design_choices: A shallow cave under a tan limestone overhang in rocky Judean hill country, dotted with scrub and wild thyme.
Bright afternoon sun outside, cool shade inside the hollow; distant walls of Jerusalem on a ridge.
locked_traits: Tan limestone overhang and scrubby hillside in every panel.

scriptural_facts.text: After three days in the wilderness Lehi pitched his tent in a valley by the side of a river of water.
Lehi built an altar of stones and made an offering there.
He named the river Laman; it emptied into the Red Sea, and the valley was near its mouth.
Lehi wished Lemuel to be like the valley: firm, steadfast, and immovable.
Lehi dwelt in a tent.

visual_design_choices: A steep-walled desert valley of rose-red and ochre granite cliffs opening toward a glimpse of the blue Red Sea.
A clear stream (the river Laman) runs along the valley floor, lined with bright green date palms, reeds, and acacia.
Lehi's camp: several large goat-hair tents in dark brown and black stripes, with camels and a low altar of piled unhewn stones.
Brilliant desert sunlight, deep blue sky, strong shadows.
locked_traits: Red-and-ochre cliffs, palm-lined stream, and striped goat-hair tents in every panel.
The altar is always rough unhewn stones.

scriptural_facts.text: Four days' travel south-southeast, the family pitched tents at a place they named Shazer.
From Shazer they hunted with bows and arrows, keeping to the most fertile parts of the wilderness near the Red Sea.

visual_design_choices: An Arabian desert oasis camp: goat-hair tents beside a small grove of palms and thorny acacia with patches of green grass.
Golden dunes and rocky hills on the horizon; wide bright sky.
locked_traits: Oasis palms and striped tents; desert Arabia, not jungle.

scriptural_facts.text: Ishmael died and was buried in the place called Nahom.

visual_design_choices: A wide, dry Arabian plain ringed by bare rocky hills, with a low burial cairn of piled stones.
Late-afternoon golden light and a pale blue sky; solemn but not dark.
locked_traits: Burial cairn of stacked stones on an open plain.

scriptural_facts.text: The family named the land Bountiful because of its much fruit and wild honey.
They beheld the sea, which they called Irreantum, meaning many waters, and pitched tents by the seashore.
Nephi went up into a mountain there to pray.

visual_design_choices: A lush green coastal pocket on the southern Arabian shore: fruit trees, tall palms, wild figs, and flowering shrubs humming with bees.
A white sand beach and turquoise sea; a steep green-and-grey mountain rises behind the camp.
Goat-hair tents near the beach; a shipbuilding site with cut timbers and a small forge for smelting ore.
Vivid tropical color, bright sun, deep blue sea and sky.
locked_traits: Green coast, white beach, turquoise sea, and a mountain behind in every panel.
A welcome contrast to the desert: always lush and bright.

scriptural_facts.text: Nephi worked timbers of curious workmanship and built the ship after the manner the Lord showed him, not after the manner of men.
The workmanship of the ship was exceedingly fine.
It carried the families, provisions, and seeds and was driven by the wind toward the promised land.
At sea a great and terrible tempest drove the ship back for days.

visual_design_choices: A large, sturdy wooden sailing ship of honey-brown timber with finely fitted planks and carved curling prow and stern.
One tall mast with a broad square sail of cream woven cloth; a covered deck house; cords of palm-fiber rope.
Its shape is unique and handsome, not a Viking longship, galleon, or any recognizable historical ship.
Fair-weather scenes: sparkling blue sea and sunny sky. Storm scenes: grey-green towering waves, desaturated and dramatic.
locked_traits: Same honey-brown hull, carved curling prow, and single cream square sail in every panel.
No cannons, metal fittings, or later-era rigging.

scriptural_facts.text: In the dream Lehi first found himself in a dark and dreary waste.
He then beheld a large and spacious field and a tree whose fruit was desirable to make one happy.
The fruit was white, exceeding all whiteness he had seen.
Nephi saw that the tree's beauty was far beyond all beauty and its whiteness exceeded the driven snow.
A river of water ran near the tree; a rod of iron extended along its bank, beside a strait and narrow path that led to the tree.
An exceedingly great mist of darkness arose, and some on the path lost their way.

visual_design_choices: A radiant, dreamlike landscape: a single broad-crowned tree glowing with soft white light, heavy with luminous white fruit.
A vast green field under a luminous sky; a clear river beside the tree; a dark iron rod on low posts running beside a narrow dirt path.
Where the mist rises it rolls in as grey-black fog, desaturated around the edges, while the tree stays bright.
locked_traits: The tree always glows brilliant white; the rod of iron always runs along the path by the river.
Visionary and luminous, but still hand-inked illustration.

scriptural_facts.text: Across the river stood a great and spacious building, as it were in the air, high above the earth.
It was filled with finely dressed people, old and young, mocking and pointing at those eating the fruit.
It represents vain imaginations and the pride of the children of men.

visual_design_choices: An enormous, showy many-windowed building floating with no visible foundation, glittering with gold trim and brightly lit windows.
Tall and top-heavy, looking impressive but hollow; its brightness is gaudy and cold compared with the warm glow of the tree.
Seen from across the river, set against the dream's sky.
locked_traits: Always floating above the ground with no foundation.
Never modern glass-and-steel; an ornate, timeless, dreamlike palace.

scriptural_facts.text: After many days at sea they arrived at the promised land, went ashore, and pitched their tents.
The forests held beasts of every kind, including the cow, ox, ass, horse, goat, and wild goat, and the land held ore of gold, silver, and copper.

visual_design_choices: A tropical Pacific-side coastline of the New World: golden beach, crashing blue surf, and dense emerald jungle beyond.
Nephi's ship anchored just offshore; the family's tents in a clearing at the forest edge.
Distant green volcanic mountains under a brilliant blue sky with white clouds.
locked_traits: Lush jungle, golden beach, and blue surf: the first vivid New World landscape.
No buildings yet; only tents.

scriptural_facts.text: Nephi's people journeyed many days in the wilderness and named the place where they settled Nephi.
Nephi taught his people to build buildings and to work wood, iron, copper, brass, steel, gold, silver, and precious ores.
Later settlers repaired the walls of the city of Lehi-Nephi and the city of Shilom.
The city had walls and a gate, with a back pass through the back wall.

visual_design_choices: A highland city in a green mountain valley, with whitewashed stone-and-plaster houses and terraced maize fields on the slopes.
A stone perimeter wall with a main gate; a stepped temple platform rises at the city's heart.
Pine and oak on the surrounding hills, clear mountain air, bright blue sky.
Also called the city of Lehi-Nephi in Mosiah; same design across eras, growing grander in King Noah's time.
locked_traits: Highland valley setting with terraced fields and a walled city in every panel.
Mesoamerican-style stone architecture, never European.

scriptural_facts.text: Nephi built a temple after the manner of Solomon's temple, though not of so many precious things; its workmanship was exceedingly fine.
Jacob taught the people in the temple.
King Noah had fine work of wood, copper, and brass made within its walls, and gold-ornamented seats with a breastwork for his priests.

visual_design_choices: A rectangular stone temple on a raised stepped platform, facing east across an open courtyard with an altar.
A pillared porch at the entrance with two great freestanding columns, echoing Solomon's plan.
Pale limestone walls with turquoise-and-red painted fretwork bands; cedar doors.
In King Noah's era: added gold-leaf trim, carved wood panels, and a raised row of gilded priests' seats behind a carved breastwork.
locked_traits: Same stepped platform, two porch columns, and turquoise fretwork in every panel.
Gilded seats and breastwork appear only in King Noah's era and later.

scriptural_facts.text: King Noah built many elegant and spacious buildings ornamented with fine wood, gold, silver, iron, brass, ziff, and copper.
He built a spacious palace with a throne in its midst, of fine wood ornamented with gold, silver, and precious things.

visual_design_choices: A lavish throne room with tall carved-cedar columns inlaid with gold and silver, and a raised gold-trimmed throne at the center.
Jade-green and crimson hangings, polished stone floors, bronze braziers, and trays of fruit and wine.
Warm, glittering light; opulent and indulgent.
locked_traits: Same carved-cedar gilded columns and central gold throne in every panel.
Mesoamerican-inspired ornament, never a European royal court.

scriptural_facts.text: Noah built a very high tower near the temple, from which he could overlook the land of Shilom and the land of Shemlon.
He also built a great tower on the hill north of the land of Shilom.

visual_design_choices: A tall, narrow stepped stone tower with a railed wooden platform at the top.
Below, a sweeping view of green valleys, fields, and distant Lamanite lands under a clear blue sky.
locked_traits: Tall stepped stone tower with a wooden lookout platform.

scriptural_facts.text: Mormon was a place in the borders of the land, at times infested by wild beasts.
It had a fountain of pure water with a thicket of small trees nearby, where Alma hid by day.
The place, waters, and forest of Mormon were beautiful to those who came to know their Redeemer there.

visual_design_choices: A clear, spring-fed pool of turquoise water in a highland forest clearing, with smooth stones at the edge.
A dense thicket of slender young trees beside the water; tall trees, ferns, and flowering vines beyond.
Dappled sunlight through green leaves; peaceful, hopeful, and beautiful.
locked_traits: Same turquoise spring pool and thicket of small trees in every panel.
Always lush, serene, and bright.

scriptural_facts.text: Alma's people came to a very beautiful and pleasant land of pure water.
They pitched tents, tilled the ground, and built buildings.
They prospered exceedingly and called the land Helam.

visual_design_choices: A broad, gentle green valley with clear streams, young maize fields, and simple thatched-roof houses of timber and adobe.
Wooded hills around the valley, wildflowers, bright sun.
locked_traits: Modest thatched village among green fields and clear streams.

scriptural_facts.text: Mosiah's people came down into the land of Zarahemla and found the people of Zarahemla there.
The river Sidon ran by the land of Zarahemla.
A highway led to the chief market in the city.

visual_design_choices: The great Nephite capital on a wide river plain: plastered white and ochre stone buildings, broad plazas, and a stepped temple-pyramid at the center.
Paved raised highways (sacbe) lined with market stalls of bright woven cloth, pottery, and produce.
Palm trees, flowering trees, canals, and lush jungle edging the farmland; the river Sidon glinting nearby.
Bright tropical sun, blue sky, busy and prosperous.
locked_traits: Same central stepped temple-pyramid and white-and-ochre plazas in every panel.
Mesoamerican-style city, never European or Asian.

scriptural_facts.text: Refused entry to the city, Samuel the Lamanite climbed upon its wall to prophesy.
Angry Nephites threw stones and shot arrows at him on the wall, but could not hit him.

visual_design_choices: A thick, tall city wall of fitted pale stone with a flat walkway along its top, part of the City of Zarahemla.
Below it, a crowd-filled open ground; behind, the white-and-ochre rooftops and temple-pyramid of the city.
Bright daylight, blue sky.
locked_traits: Same pale fitted-stone wall with a flat top walkway; matches the City of Zarahemla design.

scriptural_facts.text: Nephi prayed upon a tower in his garden, by the highway leading to the chief market of Zarahemla, near the garden gate.

visual_design_choices: A walled garden of fruit trees and flowering shrubs beside a busy paved highway, with a simple wooden gate.
A modest square stone tower, a little taller than the garden wall, with a flat roof where Nephi kneels.
Bright daylight; passers-by on the highway can see the tower top.
locked_traits: Modest square stone tower near the garden gate, beside the highway.

scriptural_facts.text: The people gathered to go up to the temple to hear King Benjamin.
They pitched their tents round about the temple, each family separate, with tent doors toward the temple.
The multitude was too great to teach within the temple walls, so Benjamin had a tower erected.

visual_design_choices: A grand stepped stone temple on a wide platform, painted white with turquoise and red fretwork, enclosed by a low courtyard wall.
For King Benjamin's address: hundreds of colorful family tents in rings around the temple, every door facing it, and a tall timber speaking tower beside the wall.
Brilliant sunny day, blue sky, a festive and reverent gathering.
locked_traits: Same stepped white temple with turquoise fretwork in every panel.
Tent doors always face the temple during Benjamin's address.

scriptural_facts.text: The river Sidon ran by the land of Zarahemla.
Battles were fought on its banks, and the slain were cast into its waters.
Many were baptized in the waters of Sidon.

visual_design_choices: A wide, slow jade-green river winding through tropical lowlands, with sandy banks and tall reeds.
Dense jungle, ceiba trees, and palms along the banks; herons and bright birds.
Bright tropical sun; the river looks broad but fordable at crossings.
locked_traits: Wide jade-green river with jungle banks in every panel.

scriptural_facts.text: Ammonihah was a city three days' journey north of the land of Melek.
Its people cast believers and their scriptures into a fire.
Its people called it a great city that God could not destroy.

visual_design_choices: A proud, wealthy walled city of tall painted stone buildings, a large judgment hall, and a wide central plaza.
Crimson and gold banners and ornate carvings suggest pride and wealth.
Bright daylight; handsome on the surface.
locked_traits: Same crimson-and-gold banners and central plaza in every panel before its destruction.

scriptural_facts.text: Alma and Amulek were bound with strong cords and confined in prison, without food or water.
The earth shook, the prison walls were rent in twain and fell, killing their persecutors, while Alma and Amulek came forth unhurt.

visual_design_choices: A thick-walled stone prison with a heavy outer door and small barred window slits letting in shafts of daylight.
When the walls fall: great slabs split apart, dust in the air, and bright sunlight pouring in on Alma and Amulek.
locked_traits: Heavy stone walls with an outer door; bright light floods in when they fall.

scriptural_facts.text: In one day Ammonihah was left desolate, and every living soul of its people was destroyed.
The dead were heaped and thinly covered; the land lay desolate for many years and was called Desolation of Nehors.

visual_design_choices: The ruined shell of Ammonihah: collapsed walls, empty plazas, torn crimson banners, and weeds pushing through stone.
Low earthen mounds outside the walls; no bodies shown.
Muted and desaturated, overcast grey sky.
locked_traits: Desaturated ruin; no visible bodies or gore.

scriptural_facts.text: Ammon went to the land of Ishmael, named after the sons of Ishmael.

visual_design_choices: Lamanite pastoral lands of rolling green hills and grassland, with herds and flocks grazing.
The king's town: wooden-and-adobe buildings with palm-thatch roofs around a larger royal compound.
Bright sunny sky, lush and fertile.
locked_traits: Rolling grassland with flocks and a palm-thatched royal town.

scriptural_facts.text: Lamoni had horses and chariots prepared by his servants.

visual_design_choices: A royal compound of plastered adobe and timber with a high palm-thatch roof and carved wooden posts painted red and ochre.
The main hall has woven reed mats, feather-and-cloth hangings, and a low raised dais for the king's seat and bed.
Warm light from doorways and oil lamps; rich but not gilded.
locked_traits: Same carved red-and-ochre posts, thatched roof, and raised dais in every panel.
Lamanite royal style: less gold than Nephite palaces.

scriptural_facts.text: The water of Sebus was the place where all the Lamanites drove their flocks to drink.

visual_design_choices: A wide watering pool fed by a stream in open grassland, with trampled muddy banks and scattered boulders.
Clumps of trees, rocky rises where men could hide, and grazing flocks.
Bright midday sun, blue sky.
locked_traits: Same watering pool with boulders and muddy banks in every panel.

scriptural_facts.text: Aaron was led to the house of the king over all the land, Lamoni's father, in the land of Nephi.
Lamoni's father appointed a great feast in the land of Nephi.

visual_design_choices: The grandest Lamanite hall: a tall stone-and-timber palace on a stepped platform in the old city of Nephi, with a steep thatched roof.
Painted murals of jaguars and quetzal birds, feather fans, and a large carved stone throne.
Warm, bright interior light.
locked_traits: Carved stone throne and jaguar-and-quetzal murals in every panel.

scriptural_facts.text: A narrow strip of wilderness ran from the east sea to the west sea, dividing the land of Nephi from the land of Zarahemla.
Missionaries journeyed many days in the wilderness, fasting and praying.
Ammon's party wandered forty days in the wilderness seeking the land of Lehi-Nephi.

visual_design_choices: Rugged forested mountains and ravines: tall trees hung with moss, ferns, rushing streams, and misty ridgelines.
Narrow trails over rocks and roots; sunlight in shafts through the canopy.
locked_traits: Green, rugged, forested highlands; never desert.

scriptural_facts.text: The Zoramites lived in Antionum, east of Zarahemla near the seashore.
They built synagogues and gathered there one day each week.
In the center stood a place for standing high above the head, whose top admitted only one person.
They called it Rameumptom, the holy stand.

visual_design_choices: A tall, bright synagogue hall of polished white stone with gold-leaf trim and colored glassless windows letting in sun.
At the center, a narrow pillar-like stand with steps, rising well above head height to a small railed platform for one person.
Worshippers in costly, brightly dyed robes; the setting looks rich and proud.
locked_traits: The Rameumptom is always a single tall narrow stand at the center, top wide enough for one.
Rich, gilded, and proud in look.

scriptural_facts.text: Jershon lay on the east by the sea, joining the land Bountiful on its south, and was given to the people of Ammon.

visual_design_choices: Green coastal lowlands by the east sea: palm groves, fields, and new thatched villages of the people of Ammon.
Turquoise sea, white sand, and bright sky.
locked_traits: Peaceful coastal farmland with new villages.

scriptural_facts.text: Moroni erected small forts and places of resort, threw up banks of earth, and built walls of stone around cities and borders.
Heaps of earth were dug up around the cities, with works of timbers the height of a man on top.
A strong, high frame of pickets stood on the timbers, overlooked by towers with places of security.
A deep ditch ran round about, and the only way in was by the entrance.

visual_design_choices: A Nephite city ringed by a deep ditch and a high earthen bank, topped by a wall of timbers and sharpened pickets.
Wooden watchtowers with roofed, shielded platforms at intervals; one guarded entrance.
White-and-ochre stone buildings and a temple-pyramid visible inside; green countryside outside; bright day.
locked_traits: Ditch, earthen bank, timber-and-picket wall, and towers always appear together.
Timber and earth defenses, never European stone castles.

scriptural_facts.text: The Nephites founded the city of Moroni by the east sea, on the south by the Lamanite border.
In the great destruction it sank into the depths of the sea and its inhabitants were drowned.

visual_design_choices: A fortified seaside city of white stone on a low coastal plain, with timber-and-picket walls and a harbor of canoes.
Before the destruction: turquoise sea and bright sun. During it: grey churning water swallowing the city, desaturated.
locked_traits: Seaside white-stone city with timber defenses; desaturated only in destruction scenes.

scriptural_facts.text: A small neck of land, a day and a half's journey for a Nephite from the east to the west sea, joined the land northward and the land southward.
A narrow pass led by the sea into the land northward.

visual_design_choices: A narrow green isthmus with sea visible on both sides from high ground, jungle hills along its spine.
A rocky coastal pass squeezed between cliffs and the sea.
Bright day, blue water on both horizons.
locked_traits: Sea on both sides; a narrow pass by the shore.

scriptural_facts.text: Nephi and Lehi were cast into the same prison where Ammon's brethren had been held by Limhi's servants.
Nephi and Lehi were encircled about as if by fire, yet were not burned, and the fire did not take hold of the walls.
Their captors were overshadowed with a cloud of darkness.

visual_design_choices: A large, dim stone prison chamber with heavy walls and a single barred doorway.
When the fire appears: a ring of brilliant golden-white flame around Nephi and Lehi lighting their faces, the walls untouched, while dark cloud fills the rest of the room.
locked_traits: The fire never burns the walls or the prophets.
Bright golden light at the center, darkness around the edges.

scriptural_facts.text: The Gadianton robbers dwelt upon the mountains in strong holds and secret places that the people could not overpower.

visual_design_choices: Steep, jungle-covered mountain ridges with hidden caves, rock shelters, and camouflaged log palisades.
Rope bridges over gorges, lookout rocks, and smoky campfires.
Deep green forest and sharp sunlight; shadowy inside the hideouts.
locked_traits: Hidden caves and log palisades in steep jungle mountains.

scriptural_facts.text: People in the land northward dwelt in tents and in houses of cement, and let trees grow for later timber.
Timber was exceedingly scarce, and much was sent there by shipping.

visual_design_choices: Open, drier country of grassland and scattered young trees, with towns of smooth grey-white cement houses with flat roofs.
Stacks of shipped timber at a river landing; distant blue mountains.
Bright sun, big sky.
locked_traits: Cement houses and sparse trees; drier and more open than the lush south.

scriptural_facts.text: A great storm arose, such as never had been known, with a great and terrible tempest and thunder that shook the whole earth.
The city of Zarahemla took fire.
The highways were broken up, level roads spoiled, and smooth places made rough.
The face of the whole earth was deformed by tempests, thunderings, lightnings, and earthquakes; the rocks were rent into fragments, seams, and cracks.

visual_design_choices: Nephite lands torn apart: split and buckled paved highways, collapsed stone buildings, and cracked ground.
Jagged lightning, whirlwinds, sheets of rain, and fires glowing orange against a black-green sky.
Desaturated and dramatic per the global style: storm greys and deep shadow, with lightning and fire the only bright color.
locked_traits: This is the one kind of scene that stays desaturated and dark.
No gore; destruction is shown through buildings, land, and sky.

scriptural_facts.text: In the great destruction the earth was carried up upon the city of Moronihah, and in its place there became a great mountain.

visual_design_choices: Where a city stood, a raw new mountain of torn earth and broken rock rises, with only a few stone rooftops at its foot.
Stormy, desaturated grey sky with lightning.
locked_traits: A new raw-earth mountain where the city was; desaturated storm scene.

scriptural_facts.text: King Jacob's people fled to the northernmost part of the land and built a kingdom.
That great city Jacobugath was burned with fire because of their wickedness and secret combinations.

visual_design_choices: A dark, fortified stronghold city of black-and-red painted stone in the far north, with high walls and a fortress-palace.
When burning: consumed in towering orange flame against a black sky.
locked_traits: Black-and-red painted stone fortress city.

scriptural_facts.text: Thick darkness covered the land, and the people could feel the vapor of darkness.
No candle, torch, or fire could be kindled, and neither sun, moon, nor stars could be seen, for three days.
On the third morning the darkness dispersed, and the earth ceased to tremble.

visual_design_choices: Near-total blackness drawn as heavy inky texture, with only the faintest silhouettes of huddled people and ruined walls.
No light sources at all: no torches, fires, or sky glow.
Readable only through subtle dark-blue and grey ink modeling.
locked_traits: Never show any light source during the three days of darkness.
Desaturated and dark per the global style's darkness exception.

scriptural_facts.text: A great multitude gathered round about the temple in the land Bountiful, marveling at the great change that had taken place.
They saw a Man descending out of heaven, clothed in a white robe, who stood in their midst.

visual_design_choices: A broad stepped stone temple-pyramid on a wide plaza, painted white with turquoise fretwork.
Recent earthquake damage: long cracks through the plaza paving and some tumbled stones at the base, but the temple stands.
Fresh, clear morning after the darkness: washed blue sky, bright sun, glistening green trees all around.
Hopeful and radiant; the brightest, most reverent setting in the book.
locked_traits: Same white stepped temple with turquoise fretwork and cracked plaza in every panel.
Always bright and hopeful after the darkness.

scriptural_facts.text: The disciples went down unto the water's edge, and the multitude followed.
They were baptized and came up out of the water.

visual_design_choices: A clear, calm river near the temple at Bountiful, with a gently sloping pebbled bank and reeds.
Palms and flowering trees; the temple's top visible over the trees; bright sunny sky.
locked_traits: Calm clear water with a gentle bank near the temple.

scriptural_facts.text: Mormon gathered his people to the land of Cumorah, by a hill called Cumorah, for the final battle.
They pitched tents around the hill in a land of many waters, rivers, and fountains.
Mormon hid the records in the hill Cumorah, except the plates given to Moroni.
It was the same hill the Jaredites called Ramah, where Coriantumr's army camped.

visual_design_choices: A single prominent, rounded, grass-and-forest-covered hill rising above lowlands threaded with rivers, lakes, and springs.
Before battle: tents ringing the base, bright sky and gleaming waters.
After battle: an empty, wind-swept field under an overcast sky; no bodies or gore shown.
locked_traits: Same rounded hill surrounded by many waters in every panel, for both the Nephite and Jaredite endings.

scriptural_facts.text: Ammaron deposited the sacred engravings in a hill called Shim in the land Antum.

visual_design_choices: A rocky, wooded hill with a concealed stone-lined cave entrance behind brush.
Inside, stacked records and plates on stone ledges.
Bright day outside, cool shade within.
locked_traits: Concealed cave entrance in a rocky wooded hill.

scriptural_facts.text: Limhi's explorers found a land among many waters covered with bones of men and beasts and ruins of buildings of every kind.
It had been peopled and destroyed, and was covered with dry bones.

visual_design_choices: Overgrown ruins of large stone buildings among lakes and marshes, with sun-bleached scattered bones in the grass.
Green vines climbing broken walls; bright but eerie light.
locked_traits: Overgrown ruins among many waters; bones are bleached and old, never gory.

scriptural_facts.text: Jared and his brother came forth from the great tower at the time the Lord confounded the language of the people.

visual_design_choices: An immense, unfinished stepped mud-brick ziggurat in a flat Mesopotamian plain, rising in tiers with ramps and scaffolds.
Tan and ochre brick, date palms and canals below, hot bright sun and hazy sky.
Old World Mesopotamian architecture, not Mesoamerican.
locked_traits: Tiered mud-brick ziggurat on a flat plain; Mesopotamian, not Mesoamerican.

scriptural_facts.text: Jared, his brother, their families and friends went down into the valley northward called Nimrod, with flocks of every kind.

visual_design_choices: A broad green river valley between dry hills, with grazing flocks, tents, and gathered animals and seeds.
Bright sun, blue sky, Old World Near Eastern landscape.
locked_traits: Green river valley between dry hills; Old World setting.

scriptural_facts.text: At the great sea the Jaredites pitched their tents, called the place Moriancumer, and dwelt in tents on the seashore for four years.

visual_design_choices: A long pale beach camp with many large tents, livestock pens, and barges under construction on the sand.
Deep blue sea, gentle surf, bright sky.
locked_traits: Seashore tent camp with barges being built.

scriptural_facts.text: The brother of Jared went up mount Shelem, named for its exceeding height.
He moltened sixteen small stones out of rock, white and clear as transparent glass, and carried them to the top.

visual_design_choices: An exceedingly tall, steep rocky mountain above the sea, its summit a bare stone crown above the clouds.
Brilliant clear sky at the top, sea far below.
locked_traits: Towering steep peak above the clouds by the sea.

scriptural_facts.text: There were eight vessels.
The barges were small and light upon the water, like a fowl.
They were tight like a dish on bottom, sides, top, and door; the ends were peaked; each was the length of a tree.
Each had a hole in the top and in the bottom that could be unstopped for air.
The Lord made the stones shine, one in each end of each vessel, to give light.
A furious wind drove them toward the promised land; they were often buried in the depths by mountain waves.

visual_design_choices: Enclosed, dish-tight wooden vessels with peaked ends, rounded tops, a sealed door, and a stoppered hole in the top.
About the length of one tall tree; no sails or oars.
Inside, a glowing white stone at each end lights people, animals, and food stores with a soft steady glow.
Calm scenes: bright blue sea. Storm scenes: huge dark waves, desaturated, with the barges' glow the only light.
locked_traits: Eight identical barges; peaked ends, fully enclosed, no sails or oars.
Interior always lit by one white glowing stone at each end.

scriptural_facts.text: Moron, where the Jaredite king dwelt, was near the land the Nephites called Desolation.

visual_design_choices: A Jaredite royal city of massive, rough-hewn stone halls on a fertile plain with fields and herds.
Heavy carved stone thrones and bronze ornaments; bright sky and golden fields.
locked_traits: Massive rough-hewn stone halls; older and heavier in style than Nephite cities.

scriptural_facts.text: Cast out, Ether hid in the cavity of a rock by day and went out by night to view what came upon the people.
There he finished his record.

visual_design_choices: A small cave in a cliff face overlooking a wide valley, with a plain stone ledge used as a writing desk.
By night: deep blue moonlight and distant campfires in the valley below, still clear and readable.
locked_traits: Cliffside cave with a view over the valley.

scriptural_facts.text: Many Lamanites dwelt in tents and wandered in the wilderness.
The more idle part of the Lamanites lived in tents in the wilderness on the west, bordering the seashore.

visual_design_choices: Hide tents clustered in a jungle clearing near the western coast, with drying racks, cooking fires, and bows leaning on posts.
Tall palms and broadleaf jungle, bright sun.
locked_traits: Hide tents in a jungle clearing; no permanent buildings.

scriptural_facts.text: Enos went to hunt beasts in the forests.

visual_design_choices: A deep, tall highland forest of oak, pine, and broadleaf trees, with mossy trunks, ferns, and wild game trails.
Shafts of warm sunlight through the canopy; lush greens.
locked_traits: Lush highland forest with sunbeams; never gloomy.
